newsitem.title: USA: PageNet sees VoiceNow hurting cash flow.
newsitem.headline: PageNet sees VoiceNow hurting cash flow.

text.p: Paging Network Inc, the largest U.S. paging firm, said that costs of its new service VoiceNow cut cash flow by $6.45 million in the first 1997 quarter, but is seen cash-flow positive in its second year.
VoiceNow, a pager which can receive voice messages, is still expected to hurt cash flow by $30 million to $40 million for its first 12 months as predicted, it said.

PageNet, which earlier on Thursday reported a wider loss per share of $0.39 in the first quarter from $0.12 a year ago, said it expected 1997 per share losses would be significantly higher in 1997 because of accelerated depreciation.
The accelerated depreciation, of $0.08 per share, applies to pagers. The company started amortizing licenses for wireless spectrum and other costs for VoiceNow this year too.

PageNet said operating cashflow in the first quarter after accounting for VoiceNow was $64.28 million compared with $61.06 million a year ago, and its operating cashflow margin was 33.2 percent from 37.5 percent a year ago.
VoiceNow has been offered in the Dallas-Fort Worth area since late March. A nationwide rollout is due later in the year.
PageNet said its total pagers in service rose to 9.52 million in the first quarter from 7.3 million a year ago. (( Nick Louth, New York Newsroom 212 859 1712))
